newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina to ask Spain about 'Dirty War' files.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to ask Spain about 'Dirty War' files.

text.p: Argentina said on Thursday it will ask Spain for information about reports that files on the military's "Dirty War" of the late 1970s were microfilmed by Spanish intelligence and are hidden in a Swiss bank vault.
"We will see about this immediately, I am going to talk to my Spanish colleague," said Foreign Minister Guido Di Tella.
"I know nothing, but we are going to ask for information," said Interior Minister Carlos Corach.

Spanish newspaper El Mundo said leaders of Argentina's military, which ruled with an iron fist after a 1976 coup, wanted to get military files on the repression out of the country before democracy was restored in 1983 and flew eight trunks of papers from Buenos Aires to Madrid.

Spanish military intelligence agency CESID microfilmed the records before they were taken in trucks to a Swiss bank vault where they remain, the paper said. The files reportedly list thousands of suspected leftists abducted and murdered in the Argentine military's "Dirty War" campaign of terror.

El Mundo quoted an Argentine officer saying in 1983, the year Raul Alfonsin became president in democratic elections: "Two Hercules jets took off from Argentina, each with a set of the papers to safeguard against an accident or sabotage."
The military has denied such files exist and even popular current army chief Gen. Martin Balza denied it in his historic "mea culpa" in 1995 for the army's role in the Dirty War.
Alfonsin, who put the military on trial for their crimes only to see them pardoned by his successor Carlos Menem in 1989, told reporters he knew nothing of the microfilms.
"I acted correctly, I don't know what this could be about," he said.
Human rights groups say up to 30,000 people "disappeared" and they insist the military must hand over information so they can know for sure the fate of their loved ones.

Spanish judge Baltasar Garzon, who is investigating the disappearance of about 300 Spanish citizens in the Dirty War, sent a commission to investigate the safe deposits and accounts of Argentine military leaders in 1996.
Last month, Garzon issued an international arrest warrant for former Argentine military president Leopoldo Galtieri for his alleged role in the killing of three Spaniards.
